title: Building a House in the Rainy Season 2027: Technical and Safety Notes
desc: Building in the rainy season: protecting the excavation, fresh concrete, storing cement and steel, electrical safety, scaffolding and duties to neighbors.
summary: Technical and safety notes for building during the rainy season: excavation pits, concrete pours, material storage, site electricity, scaffolding and neighboring buildings.
body: p

Many families have to start construction in the rainy season because of schedule, finances or an auspicious date. Building in the rainy season is still possible, but without suitable measures it easily affects the quality of the foundation and concrete and the safety of workers. Under the regulations, the contractor must have measures to limit harm to people and property when an unsafe incident occurs (Clause 2, Article 50 of the Construction Law 2025), while the homeowner is responsible for the safety of the building, adjacent buildings and the environment during construction (Point b, Clause 3, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).
h2
1. Excavation pit: drainage and holding the walls
ul

Water standing in the excavation for a long time softens the soil at the foundation base and reduces its bearing capacity. Collection ditches, sumps and pumps are needed to pump out all the water and clear the mud before pouring blinding concrete.
Do not leave an excavated pit untouched through several rainstorms; dig only as far as you can build the foundation.

Pit walls dug close to the neighbor's house easily collapse when the soil becomes saturated. Support measures must be calculated by a qualified person based on the actual geology – this is a common error that leads to settlement and cracking of the adjoining house, see Construction causing settlement or cracks in a neighbor's house: who pays compensation?.
h2
2. Pouring concrete when it rains
ul

Follow the weather forecast and avoid pouring foundation, floor or roof concrete in heavy rain. Rain on freshly poured concrete washes away the cement paste and increases the water content, making the concrete less dense.
Have tarpaulins ready to cover the area being poured. If rain comes suddenly, cover immediately and let the engineer decide to stop at a suitable construction joint, not stop arbitrarily.
After pouring, cover to protect the surface; once the rain stops, moist curing must still be carried out as technically required.

If concrete has a surface damaged by rain or its quality is in doubt, notify the engineer to inspect; for load-bearing elements, testing may be needed. The homeowner has the right to stop construction and require the contractor to remedy when quality regulations are violated (Point c, Clause 1, Article 59 of the Construction Law 2025).
h2
3. Storing materials
ul
Cement: raise it off the ground, cover it fully, and keep it away from damp walls; bags that have lumped have absorbed moisture and must not be used for structures.
Steel reinforcement: keep on racks and cover with tarpaulin. Steel with flaking rust scale should be cleaned or rejected as the engineer directs before tying.
Bricks, sand and stone: bricks that absorb too much water easily cause mortar to run when laid; sand washed by water and mixed with mud and soil should be rechecked.
p
Materials must meet the design requirements (Clause 4, Article 50 of the Construction Law 2025) – see Building materials must be conformity-certified: what should the homeowner check?.
h2
4. Electrical safety, scaffolding and work at height
ul
Construction electricity must have switching devices and electric shock protection; wires should be hung high, not lie in puddles, and sockets should be shielded.

Scaffolding and working platforms are slippery in rain: check scaffold feet and ties before each shift. Scaffolding and temporary support structures are items the homeowner needs to supervise (Point c, Clause 4, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026).
Stop work at height and on the roof during thunderstorms, lightning or strong wind. Workers have the right to refuse work that is not safe (Clause 3, Article 17 of Decree 207/2026).
h2
5. Roof, walls and waterproofing
ul
Prioritize finishing the roof and temporarily covering openings before the peak of the rains, to protect interior finishes.
Newly built walls in heavy rain need their tops covered; do not plaster or paint while the wall is still too damp.
The rainy season is a good time to test water and detect leaks at gutters, the roof and the joints against the neighboring house before acceptance.
h2
6. Planning a reasonable schedule
p

When signing a contract for the rainy season, it is advisable to clearly agree on schedule adjustments for unusual weather and on responsibility for covering and storing materials. Do not rush the schedule by pouring concrete or removing formwork before technical conditions are met.
p
If you plan to start construction in the rainy season and need suitable construction methods prepared, please contact Quan Construction for advice.
note

This article is for reference; each building needs a survey and design by a qualified person. Construction methods, support of excavations and the time to remove formwork must be decided by the engineer according to the design and actual conditions.
